subject: ALIGNED clause
notes: 'aligned on the first bit of the first available byte boundary. Implicit filler bits may be generated ... as described in 8.5.1.6.3.' One conjunct on THE one placement predicate: an ALIGNED subject never shares its predecessor's byte, and the round-up every caller already performs does the rest. The predicate was previously written out THREE times - BitLayout.ExtentBits, BitLayout.StartBitWithin and DataBinder.AssignClassOffsets - and is now a single method all three call, so an item's OFFSET, the group's EXTENT and a REDEFINES view of it cannot disagree. Golden derivation: 05 B1 PIC 1(4) BIT. 05 B2 PIC 1(4) BIT ALIGNED. occupies 12 bits padded by rule 4 to 16, so FUNCTION LENGTH is 2 where without ALIGNED it is 1 - measured 2.
